Update and mitigation summary (internal + customer-facing):

Timeline:
- 2026-12-01 08:46 PST — error-rate and latency alerts triggered on df-09 clusters.
- 2026-12-01 09:10 PST — confirmed intermittent SERVFAIL from customer DNS lookups for regional LB.
- 2026-12-01 10:02 PST — increased connection resets and ephemeral port exhaustion observed on dedicated egress NAT (us-west-2).
- 2026-12-02 02:12 PST — rolled temporary route fallback to secondary region for affected flows; reduced error rate from ~22% to ~3% for impacted routes.
- 2026-12-02 14:30 PST — applied conntrack tuning and increased SNAT port range on dedicated NAT appliances.
- 2026-12-03 16:30 PST — implemented permanent firewall rule rollback (policy 374) that had silently tightened during a config automation push on 2026-11-30.

Root cause (summary):
- A recent automation pull (policy 374) tightened outbound firewall state timeouts and unintentionally caused asymmetric NAT sessions for certain high-throughput clients. The tighter timeouts caused early session termination which, combined with aggressive client retries, produced a retry storm and ephemeral port exhaustion on the dedicated NAT, leading to elevated 5xx/429 and connection timeouts. Secondary DNS failures were a symptom of overloaded control-plane paths rather than primary cause.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back the firewall policy for affected Dedicated pools (completed 2026-12-03 16:30 PST).
- Expanded SNAT port range and adjusted conntrack thresholds to handle high-throughput reconciliation jobs.
- Deployed a short-term routing policy that favors multi-region fallback for customers with critical payment SLAs (BigFintech included).
- Added a customer-facing recommended retry/backoff doc for BigFintech and engineering teams to reduce amplification during spikes.

Customer-facing note (short):
Hi Priya / Arjun — apologies for the disruption. We identified an automated firewall policy change that tightened NAT/session timeouts and triggered a retry amplification against your flows. We have rolled back the change, expanded SNAT capacity, and provisioned a multi-region fallback while we harden our automation and add guardrails to prevent recurrence. Our SRE and your ops team can coordinate a traffic cutover window if you prefer to test in a non-production window.

Requested next steps for execs:
- Laura: can you please share the short executive summary to Arjun and BigFintech leadership and offer a one-week SLA credit as discussed?
- Olga: please lead the customer update thread and attach the mitigation timeline PDF (attached).
- Karthik: follow up with infra automation to add a policy-change alert and staged rollout gating.
